name: Thymosin alpha-1
lead: Thymosin alpha-1 is a 28-amino-acid peptide first isolated from thymus tissue. Its synthetic form, thymalfasin, is approved as an immune modulator in a number of countries (not by the US FDA) for conditions such as chronic hepatitis B and as an adjunct in other settings.

It appears in longevity and biohacking discussions as an "immune optimizer," but its human research concerns medical conditions such as infections, sepsis and cancer adjunct care, not appearance. There is no good evidence of cosmetic benefit.

paras: Thymosin alpha-1 is thought to act on Toll-like receptors on dendritic cells and other immune cells, promoting T-cell maturation and cytokine signaling that enhances adaptive immune responses.

In clinical studies it is generally well tolerated, with mild injection-site reactions most common, but trial quality is heterogeneous and safety reporting inconsistent. Immune stimulation is a concern in autoimmune disease or transplant settings. Gray-market products are unregulated, and use in healthy people lacks supporting evidence.
